atoms.text:
Kneecap is a semi-fictional comedy-drama about the rise of the real Belfast hip-hop trio Kneecap. The story follows music teacher JJ as he teams up with rebellious friends Naoise and Liam to create an Irish-language rap group that quickly becomes a symbol of youth culture and language activism in Northern Ireland.
As the trio gains popularity, they clash with police, politicians, and paramilitary influences. Finally, Kneecap's music becomes even more popular despite the Protestant establishment doing everything in their power to stop them and the characters continue to spread knowledge about the Irish language and their identity.
The film mixes humour, political commentary, and energetic music to explore Irish identity, post-Troubles Belfast, and efforts to preserve the Irish language.

atoms.title: Regional identity & the role of past conflicts

atoms.text: The characters are shaped by the legacy of The Troubles, even though they belong to a younger, post-conflict generation. Old political and cultural divisions still influence how they see themselves and how others perceive them. Rather than directly reliving the conflict, the characters inherit its consequences: marginalisation, identity confusion, and tension with authority.

example.a: In short: the past conflict is not gone—it lingers in language, culture, and everyday life.
example.sound: In short: the past conflict is not gone—it lingers in language, culture, and everyday life.

atoms.text: Irish or Irish Gaelic is a Celtic language spoken in Ireland before the English enforced English as the primary language and forbid Irish to be taught in schools.

example.a: In Kneecap, Irish is a linguistic, political and cultural aspect of (Northern) Irish identity.

atoms.text: The majority of the Northern Irish population no longer has any knowledge of the Irish language but since 2022 it is an official language of Northern Ireland.
